chapter.title: Processors
chapter.para: Each VM is given physical CPUs of its own. The hypervisor runs the guests with the virtualization of the processor (AMD SVM on x86_64, exception level 2 on arm64) and handles what a guest cannot do itself.

section.title: SRQ_HV_CPU_001
section.para: The hypervisor shall give each virtual CPU (vCPU) a physical CPU of its own, in the order of the configuration, so that the VMs share no CPU time, and shall need as many physical CPUs as the VMs have vCPUs in all.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Spatial and temporal isolation of the VMs.

section.title: SRQ_HV_CPU_002
section.para: The hypervisor shall start the physical CPUs that it needs besides the one that it was started on: on x86_64 by INIT and start-up interrupts, to the CPUs that the ACPI tables list; on arm64 by the PSCI call CPU_ON, to the CPUs that the device tree lists.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Only the boot CPU runs when the hypervisor starts.

section.title: SRQ_HV_CPU_003
section.para: The hypervisor shall run the guest of the first vCPU of each VM on its CPU, and shall park the other vCPUs of the VM, halting their CPUs, because JetOS uses one CPU.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The CPUs are reserved for a JetOS that supports several.

section.title: SRQ_HV_CPU_004
section.para: The hypervisor shall show the guest one CPU: on x86_64 by the CPUID instruction, which gives the values of the host without SVM, the local APIC, x2APIC, MONITOR and the topology, with one CPU, with the bit that tells that a hypervisor is present and with a vendor leaf of the hypervisor; on arm64 by the processor identity register, which reads as the number of the vCPU.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A guest must not try to use what the hypervisor does not give it.

section.title: SRQ_HV_CPU_005
section.para: The hypervisor shall run a guest directly on the processor, and shall take control only for what the guest cannot do itself: on x86_64 the physical interrupts, port access, CPUID, the model specific registers, halt, a triple fault, the nested page faults, and the virtualization instructions, INVLPGA, MONITOR and MWAIT, for which the guest gets an invalid opcode exception; on arm64 the physical interrupts, the hypervisor and secure monitor calls, the aborts of the stage 2 translation, the wait instructions (which go on), system errors and exceptions from 32-bit code.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The guest runs at full speed, and the hypervisor stays in control.

section.title: SRQ_HV_CPU_006
section.para: The hypervisor shall emulate the model specific registers of a guest on x86_64: the extended feature register (without SVM), the time stamp counter, the page attribute table, the system call registers and the segment base registers work; all others read as zero and ignore writes, and the first access to each of the first 16 of them is reported.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A guest can run with the registers that it uses, and nothing else.

section.title: SRQ_HV_CPU_007
section.para: The hypervisor shall halt the CPU of a stopped or parked vCPU, with its interrupts off.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A CPU that has no guest to run must not disturb the others.
